children: Australian shares inched higher on Thursday, as gains in financials outweighed losses in heavyweight miners, while hot inflation data increased bets for a fifth central bank rate hike this year.
rose 0.2% to 8,868.20 as of 0105 GMT. The benchmark ended flat on Wednesday.
Wednesday data showed higher fuel-cost-driven inflation accelerating in the third quarter, strengthening expectations of a rate hike at the Reserve Bank of Australia's meeting next week.
RBA Governor Michele Bullock said policymakers will weigh next week whether four rate hikes this year are enough to rein in inflation.
Markets imply nearly nearly 85% chance of a quarter-point rise at the central bank's November 3 meeting, up from 60% before the data was released.

The central bank kept the cash rate steady at 2.75% on Wednesday. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand Governor Anna Breman said chances of a December cash rate hike are "high", but will depend on the economic outlook and how inflation is evolving.
